hints: Look closely at what each cell can actually do: can it still divide by mitosis, and does it even have a nucleus to transcribe from?
Remember telomerase is only worth making in high amounts if a cell needs many more mitotic cycles ahead of it, like during clonal expansion.
walkthrough:
**Recall what telomerase is for**

Think of telomeres as protective caps on chromosomes that get a little shorter each mitosis.

Telomerase rebuilds them, so it is only needed at high levels in cells that must keep dividing many times without ageing.

**Check cells 1 and 2 for division and transcription**

Neutrophils are terminally differentiated phagocytes. They do not divide again and live only a few days.

Mature red blood cells in mammals have lost their nucleus. With no DNA, they cannot transcribe any mRNA for telomerase at all.

**Check cell 3 for future divisions**

Activated memory T-lymphocytes must divide very rapidly by mitosis to make a large clone of effector cells on re-infection.

To survive those many cycles without losing important genes, they transcribe a high concentration of telomerase. So only 3 qualifies, which is option D.

options.A: Both 1 and 2 are wrong. Neutrophils do not divide further, and mature red blood cells have no nucleus to transcribe telomerase.
options.B: Although 3 is correct, 1 is incorrect because neutrophils are short-lived, non-dividing cells with low telomerase.
options.C: 1 alone is wrong. Neutrophils are terminally differentiated and will die by apoptosis, so they do not maintain telomeres.
options.D: Only 3 is correct. Activated memory T-lymphocytes need many rounds of mitosis in clonal expansion, so high telomerase protects their telomeres.
